chunks: Regarding the false testifier, he said: If the thing remains intact exactly as it was, it is returned to its owner; and if it no longer remains intact, he is liable for the measure of what was destroyed from the wealth of the man.

key_terms.أُتْلِفَ: Was destroyed/wasted — the diminishment or loss of the property
key_terms.شَاهِدُ الزُّورِ: False witness/perjurer — one who gives false testimony in a legal proceeding
key_terms.ضَمِنَ: He is liable/guarantees — the legal obligation to make financial restitution
key_terms.قَائِماً بِعَيْنِهِ: Remaining exactly as it was — the legal concept of the thing being identifiable and intact

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a false witness in Islamic law regarding property restitution?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) lays down the jurisprudential ruling concerning a false witness (shahid al-zur): if the property in dispute still exists in its original state, it must be restored to its rightful owner. However, if the property has been destroyed or consumed as a result of the false testimony, the perjurer bears financial liability equal to the amount of wealth destroyed. This ruling reflects the Islamic principle that wrongdoing creates restitutive obligations proportional to the harm caused.
